item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在International Republican Institute -- United States官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
IRI Announces Arrival of Delegation to Observe Par…

发布源: International Republican Institute -- United States | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

Cotabato City, ThePhilippines– The International Republican Institute (IRI), a non-profit, non-partisan organization dedicated to advancing democracy and freedom globally, is deploying a delegation of international election observers to the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) from September 10 to 15, 2026, to assess the conduct of the September 14 parliamentary elections.

“As the BARMM prepares to hold its first parliamentary elections, this historic vote marks an important milestone in the Bangsamoro peace process and an important test of the region’s democratic institutions,” said IRI Vice Chairman Randy Scheunemann, who is leading the mission. “Credible elections will help strengthen representative government, support long-term stability, and foster lasting democratic progress.”

The delegation will meet with a broad range of stakeholders, including election authorities, political parties, and civil society organizations. The mission will examine key aspects of the electoral process, including the security environment, legal framework, election administration, political and campaign environment, and opportunities for meaningful participation.

In the weeks following the mission, IRI will release a statement and report offering an impartial assessment of the quality and conduct of the elections, along with recommendations to strengthen future electoral processes.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在International Republican Institute -- United States官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
IRI Concludes Pre-Election Assessment Mission Ahea…

发布源: International Republican Institute -- United States | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

Abuja,Nigeria– The International Republican Institute (IRI) completed a pre-election assessment mission to Nigeria ahead of the country’s 2027 general elections. The mission assessed the current electoral and security environment, preparations for the general elections, and key issues that could affect peaceful and meaningful participation in the electoral process. IRI’s full statement of findings and recommendations is availablehere.

The delegation was co-led by IRI President Daniel Twining and National Endowment for Democracy Board Member and former Assistant Secretary for African Affairs Ambassador Jendayi Frazer.

“The real measure of this election will be whether Nigerians believe that peaceful political participation can determine their country’s future,” said Twining. “Violence, intimidation, and distrust cannot become substitutes for democratic competition. Nigeria’s leaders and institutions have a responsibility to protect the space in which citizens can make a genuine choice.”

IRI’s assessment was informed by its observation of the Ekiti off-cycle gubernatorial election in June and the Osun off-cycle gubernatorial election in August, as well as the work of two long-term election analysts deployed in Nigeria since July. Together, these activities provided IRI with a broader view of electoral preparations and the political environment ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Government overreach can be subtle or sweeping, but either way, it threatens the dignity and freedom of individuals. Atlas Network supports partners who push back against coercive laws, arbitrary enforcement, and unchecked state power. From fighting corruption and censorship to protecting property rights and due process, these partners are advancing reforms that strengthen the rule of law and protect individual liberty.

Only35% of the world’s population lives in a country considered “free,”according to Freedom House.

Countries with weak rule of law tend to suffer from systemic corruption, according to the World Justice Project.

Authoritarian regimes often target peaceful dissenters, imprisoning critics and restricting civil society, a trend documented in global freedom assessments.

Atlas Network increases global prosperity by strengthening a network of independent partner organizations that promote individual freedom and are committed to identifying and removing barriers to human flourishing. Since our founding in 1981, we’ve supported the development and success of pro-freedom organizations in more than 100 countries that have stood at the forefront of movements to free people from the poverty-creating policies of coercive governments.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在7. Institute for Security Studies – South Africa官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
10 Sep 2026 / by Bram Verelst & Nicodemus MindeWill monitoring of eastern DRC’s ‘ceasefire’ improve compliance?The first deployment of the monitoring mechanism is positive, but current conflict conditions should temper expectations.

发布源: 7. Institute for Security Studies – South Africa | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

Published on 10 September 2026 inISS Today

ByBram VerelstSenior Researcher, Conflict Prevention, Management and Peacebuilding in the Great Lakes Region, ISSNicodemus MindeResearcher and adjunct faculty member at United States International University – Africa, Nairobi

The first mission to verify the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) ceasefire agreed in November 2025 began its work in South Kivu on 24 August. But can facts be established in a fragmented and polarised context? And can the mission’s findings change how warring parties assess the costs, risks and benefits of continued fighting?

The Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus (EJVM+) was activated following August talks in Switzerland between the DRC government and Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC)/M23. Qatar, the United States (US) and African Union (AU) helped mediate.

Kickstarting the EJVM+ is one of the most tangible signs of progress under the Doha framework, providing a way to verify alleged ceasefire violations by the DRC government and AFC/M23.

The AfD uses symbols and rhetoric to lay claim to East Germany’s democratic revolution while borrowing governing instincts from the authoritarian state it condemned. A recent rally exposed that contradiction—and the limits of “Ostalgie” as the party pushes for power in the East.

The Alternative for Germany (AfD) is known for invoking the past to advance its future. Prominent members have beenconvicted of using Nazi slogansin speeches, and the partyregularly co-opts rhetoric from the 1989 Peaceful Revolutionthat ended communist rule in East Germany, painting itself as the modern torchbearer against an unjust system. The AfD has been thecountry’s most popular partyin the polls for several months, but its stronghold remains in the eastern states that comprised the former German Democratic Republic (GDR), where decades of state repression and undemocratic processes continue to impact politics. With elections next month in two of those states, Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the AfD sees an opportunity to finally net a seat at the governing table. In Saxony-Anhalt,the party leads the polls, with 41%, putting an absolute majority within reach.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) – United States官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
The Lessons of September 11

发布源: Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) – United States | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

Council on Foreign Relations

What can we learn from how the United States reacted to the September 11 attacks?

I have been pondering that question as the twenty-fifth anniversary of one of the darkest days in U.S. history approaches. Nearly 3,000 people died in the attacks. As many as 25,000 were injured, while thousands of first responders developed chronic and sometimes fatal illnesses.

The horror of September 11 changed the direction of U.S. foreign policy and with it the course of world events. Countering terrorismhad not been a top priorityduring the first eight months of the George W. Bush administration, even though outgoing Clinton administration officials had repeatedly warned of the threat al-Qaeda posed to U.S. interests. The Bush administration’s focus lay elsewhere, most notably in extricating the United States from agreements and diplomatic commitments it believed its predecessor had unwisely embraced.

That changed after September 11. The United States launched a “Global War on Terrorism.” Within eighteen months, the United States had invaded and toppled the governments of both Afghanistan and Iraq, begun counterterrorism operations around the world, and used its immense diplomatic and economic might to disrupt terrorist operations and cut off terrorist groups from state support.

But the war on terrorism did not produce a decisive victory akin to what the United States achieved after another surprise attack sixty years earlier, the Japanese bombing of Pearl Harb

As Africa’s largest democracy, Nigeria approaches its 2027 general elections at a pivotal moment in its—and the continent’s—democratic journey. Since 2023, the political landscape has shifted toward greater consolidation under the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) party, a weakening of the opposition People’s Democratic Party (PDP), and continued fragmentation and realignment among other opposition parties. Economic hardship, insecurity, and declining confidence in political institutions pose significant challenges to holding elections in an environment conducive to meaningful democratic participation. This includes terrorist attacks by Islamic militants, violence targeting Christian communities, intercommunal conflict targeting both Christians and Muslims, and broader ethnic tensions that have contributed to persistent insecurity across parts of the country.

Nigeria retains important foundations for democratic competition, including established electoral institutions, an active civil society, and a multiparty political system. However, political consolidation, opposition fragmentation, election-related violence, monetized political competition, and declining public trust are weakening these foundations.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) – United States官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Twenty-Five Years After 9/11, the United States Is Unprepared for Terrorism’s Next Wave

发布源: Council on Foreign Relations (CFR) – United States | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

Council on Foreign Relations

The United States marks the anniversary of the worst terrorist attack on U.S. soil with a stunning lack of preparedness to handle mounting new threats and resurgent old ones. Rapidly evolving technologies such as drones make the U.S. homeland vulnerable to attack by terror groups. Combined with the weaponization of social media by digitally savvy terrorists, the country faces the phenomenon of increasingly lethal autonomous weapons and emerging populations of radicalized youth. An eruption of violence in the Middle East triggered by the October 7, 2023, Hamas terrorist attacks on Israel and the U.S.-Israel war with Iran has further fed extremist sentiment that could be directed at the United States.

To mark the twenty-fifth anniversary, CFR Senior Fellows Bruce Hoffman and Farah Pandith have convened a special year-long comprehensive discussion series with leading experts and national security practitioners assessing the profound societal and policy effects of the 9/11 attacks. They offer their analysis on the United States’ current challenges and their recommendations on how to act.

The most pressing threat posed by terrorists and hostile actors today, and arguably across the past quarter century, comes from unmanned aerial systems (UAS): drones. The Brookings Institution is committed to supporting inclusion and diversity across all aspects of our work. We recognize that to produce high-quality research that informs innovative, practical policy recommendations, we must strive for a workplace that represents diversity of experience, thought, and personal background. This means ensuring that everyone is heard and empowered to fully participate in Brookings’ mission to equip decisionmakers with nonpartisan research and policy strategies to create a more prosperous and secure country and world.

Since 2018, we have published annually our workplace and Board of Trustee demographics. We remain optimistic that through focus, transparency, and accountability, real progress on diversity and inclusion can be achieved over the long term. These annual reports represent one component of our work toward that end.

For the past seven years, Brookings employees have shared their experiences, skills, and connections through the Brookings Mentoring Program. The program is a nine-month experience where a mid- or late-career mentor is matched with one to three early or mid-career mentees. Every year, there is wide and varied participation; over 70 employees took part in 2025, which is more than 15% of Brookings’ total employee population. Mentor groups meet monthly to discuss topics like career development and feedback and enjoy all-group programming like networking events and expert panels. The University Seminar, “Europe Since COVID-19,”is a year-long seminar series that examines the impacts of the coronavirus crisis on the European economy, politics, international relations, culture, and society.

The “Europe Since COVID-19” University Seminar is led by:

Hope M. Harrison

Professor of History and International Affairs

Kathryn Kleppinger

Associate Professor of French and Francophone Studies and International Affairs

Professor of Sociology, International Affairs, and Public Policy and Public Administration

This panel convened of two distinguished journalists and a GW political scientist with expertise in both European and American politics for a comparative post mortem of this year’s elections. On both sides of the Atlantic, partisan polarization increased, as populist and anti-immigrant issues and fallout of the Ukraine war dominated the 2024 campaigns. The speakers analyzed the commonalities and differences of the election results and in their wake, the likely course of policy and democracy.

William Drozdiak is currently a Global Fellow at the Wilson Center’s Global Europe Program. A longtime American observer of European affairs, he was the foreign editor of the Washington Post, and also served as the Post’s chief European correspondent. Global and Collective Health

发布源: BRICS Policy Center – Brazil | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

The research program “Global and Collective Health” from BRICS Policy Center aims to foster critical and integrated studies on health issues, recognizing the structural inequalities that affect populations in BRICS countries. By connecting global health dynamics with local realities, we seek to qualitatively analyze the historical, socio-environmental, economic-commercial, cultural, and digital determinants that impact well-being and the promotion of health. Through an intersectional method and approach, the program seeks to understand how different categories – gender, race, class, territory, and religion – affect access and quality of healthcare across different national and local contexts. In this sense, the program constitutes a space for interdisciplinary, interregional, and inclusive dialogue, bringing together professionals, users, social movements, and governmental entities involved in the circulation of knowledge on global and collective health.

With regional powers like Israel, Turkey, the Gulf States and Egypt, becoming increasingly assertive in the Mediterranean, this issue'sSpecial CoverageThe crowded sea: fragmentation around the Mediterranean, focuses on the role the EU could and should play in this changing landscape.

No matter how fast we run, much like in Lewis Carroll'sThrough the Looking-Glass, we struggle to catch up with AI's innovations. In ourFocusThe red queen's race: running faster to match the pace of AI, we consider how to make AI socially, economically and democratically sustainable.

Our firstDossier,Beyond implementation day: the Pact on Migration and Asylumexamines the uncertainties surrounding the pact's execution  as well as the human rights concerns raised by the approval of the Return Regulation by the European Parliament. And the secondDossierThe EU's industrial paradigm shiftfocuses on the European Commission's newly proposed Industrial Accelerator Act. Even though a noticeably more interventionist industrial strategy is proposed, the exact nature of the industrial Europe that is being shaped remains questionable.

item.content:encoded:
A Conversation with Rep. Ami Bera:Sustaining U.S.–Japan–ROK Cooperation | READ MORE >

发布源: 7. Edwin O. Reischauer Center for East Asian Studies, SAIS, Johns Hopkins University – UnitedStates | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

What does it take to maintain stability and prosperity in the Indo-Pacific over the next 75 years?

On November 20th, 2025, the Reischauer Center was honored to host Representative Ami Bera—Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on East Asia and the Pacific—for a conversation atJohns Hopkins School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS).

Representative Ami Bera stressed that, for the Indo-Pacific security in the 21st century, the US should deepen the cooperation with like-valued countries such as Japan and ROK. To strengthen U.S.–Japan–ROK trilateral ties with consistency, Representative Ami Bera believed this trilateral cooperation should be institutionalized through an ongoing legislative dialogue that can outlast political cycles.

Representative Ami Bera also explored supply-chain resilience, economic coercion, global health security, and the strategic implications of the Pacific Islands.

Grateful to Representative Bera, Dr. Calder, and to our engaged audience for this event!

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在IMANI Center for Policy and Education — Ghana官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Centre for Energy and Climate Policy

发布源: IMANI Center for Policy and Education — Ghana | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

The Centre for Energy & Climate Policyat IMANI is dedicated to finding lasting solutions to the persistent challenges in Ghana & Africa’s energy & climate sector. Despite numerous efforts to address the sector’s issues, progress has often fallen short due to a general lack of a comprehensive “follow through” approach. This underscores the need for remedial measures and their implementation to adopt a new direction and focus.

We believe that solving the energy & climate sector problems requires a multifaceted approach that includes thorough diagnosis of the sector’s issues, the development of innovative solutions, or the adoption of tried-and-tested remedial measures. Crucially, it also involves consistently tracking the implementation of these measures. This holistic approach informs our research and advocacy efforts at the Centre, ensuring that we contribute effectively to sustainable energy and climate policies in Ghana and across Africa.

Improving the Performance of State Actors in the Energy Sector-

The Centre for Energy & Climate Policy at IMANI Ghana assesses the performance of state actors in the energy sector. We evaluate public sector agencies responsible for energy based on key indicators such as transparency, efficiency, autonomy, and financial accountability. Through this comprehensive assessment, we aim to drive improvements and promote best practices within the sector, ensuring a sustainable and efficient energy landscape for Ghana and beyond.

item.title: [Singapore Institute of International Affairs (SIIA) --Singapore] [Bernama] Southern ASEAN Haze Highlights Need For Stronger Firefighting Cooperation — SIIA
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Singapore Institute of International Affairs (SIIA) --Singapore官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
[Bernama] Southern ASEAN Haze Highlights Need For Stronger Firefighting Cooperation — SIIA

发布源: Singapore Institute of International Affairs (SIIA) --Singapore | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

The current transboundary haze situation is a test of ASEAN’s preparedness and an opportunity to strengthen regional cooperation, SIIA Chairman Mr Simon Tay said in comments reported byBernama.

Mr Tay highlighted the importance of stronger cooperation to tackle fires in hotspot areas, alongside improved information-sharing and coordination of firefighting efforts. While ASEAN has made progress in hotspot monitoring and scientific data-sharing, he noted that closer cooperation will be increasingly important as the region faces hotter and drier conditions.

He also highlighted the role of the newly established ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Transboundary Haze Pollution Control (ACC THPC), expressing hope that the current haze situation would provide impetus to finalise implementation arrangements and make the centre fully operational.

Looking beyond the current dry season, Mr Tay underscored the need for sustained regional action and adequate financing for haze prevention. He noted Malaysia’s proposals at the sub-regional ASEAN ministerial meeting on haze in July for greater use of “science diplomacy” and a new Sustainable Haze Fund to strengthen regional cooperation and financing.

With climate change expected to bring hotter and drier conditions to the region, strengthening ASEAN’s capacity to prevent and respond to transboundary haze will require sustained cooperation beyond any single haze episode or dry season.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Centro de Implementacion de Politicas Publicas para la Equidad y el Crecimiento (CIPPEC) --Argentina官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Eficiencia regulatoria en ciudades y su impacto en la atracción de inversiones

发布源: Centro de Implementacion de Politicas Publicas para la Equidad y el Crecimiento (CIPPEC) --Argentina | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

Las ciudades son el lugar concreto donde la inversión se traduce en desarrollo. Según los últimos datos del Banco Mundial (2020), en ellas se genera más del 80% del producto bruto interno mundial. El resultado de las estrategias de atracción de inversiones y su posterior impacto en el desarrollo de una economía no depende solo de las condiciones macroeconómicas, sino también de la calidad institucional y la gestión local. Los gobiernos subnacionales, a través de sus regulaciones, servicios, procesos administrativos y capacidades institucionales, inciden de manera directa en las condiciones que enfrentan empresas y emprendedores.

La mayoría de los marcos conceptuales disponibles para analizar el clima de negocios han sido desarrollados a escala nacional, lo que dificulta su aplicación en el ámbito municipal. Al mismo tiempo, muchas ciudades avanzan en iniciativas concretas de mejora sin contar con herramientas sistemáticas que permitan ordenarlas, medirlas y compararlas.

En ese contexto, CIPPEC llevó adelante un proyecto, desarrollado junto al Center for International Private Enterprise (CIPE), dedicado a analizar y fortalecer la eficiencia regulatoria subnacional, tomando en cuenta las experiencias de cuatro ciudades del país de distinta escala y perfil productivo (Córdoba, Rosario, Salta y Tandil).

El 7 de septiembre, CIPPEC presentó los resultados de este estudio que constituye un punto de partida para la contribución a la mejora del entorno de inversiones local. En el even

The Brookings Institution is committed to supporting inclusion and diversity across all aspects of our work. We recognize that to produce high-quality research that informs innovative, practical policy recommendations, we must strive for a workplace that represents diversity of experience, thought, and personal background. This means ensuring that everyone is heard and empowered to fully participate in Brookings’ mission to equip decisionmakers with nonpartisan research and policy strategies to create a more prosperous and secure country and world.

Since 2018, we have published annually our workplace and Board of Trustee demographics. We remain optimistic that through focus, transparency, and accountability, real progress on diversity and inclusion can be achieved over the long term. These annual reports represent one component of our work toward that end.

For the past seven years, Brookings employees have shared their experiences, skills, and connections through the Brookings Mentoring Program. The program is a nine-month experience where a mid- or late-career mentor is matched with one to three early or mid-career mentees. Every year, there is wide and varied participation; over 70 employees took part in 2025, which is more than 15% of Brookings’ total employee population. Mentor groups meet monthly to discuss topics like career development and feedback and enjoy all-group programming like networking events and expert panels. 发布源: Hudson Institute | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

Bishkek is about to become the most consequential piece of diplomatic real estate in Eurasia.

Over three days, Kyrgyzstan's capital will host Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and, notably, only a U.S. special envoy.

The imbalance is hard to miss. Xi Jinping arrives on Aug. 30 for a state visit, during which he will also play a leading role in the Shanghai Cooperation Organization's (SCO) annual summit, while Washington sends a senior envoy to watch folk games.

On Aug. 31,SCO members and guestswill pour into the city, including Putin, Erdogan, Modi, Iranian President Masood Pezeshkian and Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif. The main SCO summit and a parallel SCO-Plus gathering will be held on Sept. 1.

Meanwhile, Aug. 31 is Kyrgyzstan’s Independence Day, marked by the opening ofBishkek Arenaand the World Nomadic Games.

It is this event that Gor, President Donald Trump’s highly active envoy, is set to attend. Gor's presence will ensure that Washington is not entirely absent from the diplomatic spotlight. He is also expected to hold separate meetings with Kazakhstan’s President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, Uzbekistan’s President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and host President Sadyr Japarov, according to a diplomatic source.

item.title: [National Bureau of Economic Research] The Bulletin on the Economics of Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在National Bureau of Economic Research官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
The Bulletin on the Economics of Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias

发布源: National Bureau of Economic Research | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

Dementia imposes substantial costs on individuals and society through healthcare expenses and caregiving needs. However, the economic consequences may begin years before clinical diagnosis, as cognitive decline can impair financial decision-making, compromise portfolio management, and increase susceptibility to fraud. InDementia and Long-Run Trajectories in Household Finances(NBER Working Paper 34659),Jing Li,Kathleen M. McGarry,Lauren Hersch Nicholas, andJonathan S. Skinneruse nearly two decades of data from the Health and Retirement Study (HRS) to compare the financial trajectories of individuals who eventually develop dementia with those of similar individuals who do not.

Household wealth begins declining approximately six years before dementia onset, primarily through impaired management of liquid financial assets.

The researchers classify individuals as having dementia when their predicted dementia probability exceeds 50 percent, capturing cognitive impairment regardless of clinical diagnosis timing. The study includes 2,312 individuals who are classified as having dementia, and 8,431 controls who are not so classified. The sample households are observed between 2000 and 2016.

发布源: National Bureau of Economic Research | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

The US capital gains tax is realization based, which means that taxes are due when appreciated assets are sold. Critics of this approach argue that it allows asset holders, such as corporate founders, to defer their tax obligations, sometimes indefinitely. An alternative approach, taxing gains on accrual, would require asset holders to value their assets periodically and to pay tax on the gain since the last valuation. Critics of this approach argue that it could force founders to surrender ownership stakes just to pay tax bills, potentially discouraging startup formation. InDilution vs. Risk Taking: Capital Gains Taxes and Entrepreneurship(NBER Working Paper 34512),Eduardo M. Azevedo,Florian Scheuer,Kent Smetters, andMin Yangexamine how shifting from realization-based to accrual-based capital gains taxation would affect venture-backed startup founders. They emphasize two effects of such a shift from realization- to accrual-based taxation: successful founders face greater ownership dilution from advance tax payments under an accrual-based scheme, while unsuccessful founders receive tax credits that function as partial insurance against downside risk.

Shifting from realization-based to accrual-based taxation of the gains on founders’ equity would dilute the stakes of those who succeed but also provide some insurance to those who fail.

Nursing homes certified by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to provide care and receive public reimbursement through Medicare and Medicaid are subject to mandatory annual inspections. While inspections are unannounced, they typically occur on an approximately yearly basis, as 74 percent of inspections take place between 40 and 60 weeks after the previous one. The average gap is around 53 weeks. Due to the cyclical nature of inspections, nursing home operators are able to anticipate when an inspection is likely and adjust their behavior accordingly. They appear to devote more effort to patient care when inspections are approaching.

InPredictably Unpredictable Inspections(NBER Working Paper 34491),Ashvin Gandhi,Andrew Olenski, andMaggie Shistudy how the predictability of nursing home inspections shapes facility effort and patient outcomes. They draw on inspection records spanning 2006 to 2019 and patient outcome data from 2013 to 2019. To measure effort, the researchers construct a composite index, drawing on payroll-based staffing variables including total hours, registered nurse hours, and full-time and overtime hours, as well as care input measures such as rates of antipsychotic use and physical restraint.

Nursing homes strategically increase care quality when an inspection is imminent. Making inspections less predictable could save almost 100 lives per year.

item.content:encoded:
Iran | United States

发布源: United States Institute of Peace (USIP) | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

On June 17, 2026, President Donald J. Trump signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Iran at the Palace of Versailles in France. The Memorandum declares an immediate and permanent termination of military operations on all fronts, including Lebanon. Both sides committed to refrain from initiating war or threatening force against one another and to respect each other’s sovereignty. The agreement opens a 60-day window, extendable by mutual consent, for negotiations toward a final deal.

Iran committed to arranging safe passage of commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, at no charge, for 60 days. Simultaneously, the United States committed to begin removing its naval blockade immediately upon signing and to fully end it within 30 days. Iran reaffirmed that it will not procure or develop nuclear weapons

The White House stated that the agreement ensures Iran will never obtain a nuclear weapon and that any sanctions relief or economic benefits are strictly contingent on Iran’s continued compliance. The State Department has since identified the memorandum as a continuing regional priority alongside efforts to secure full and free transit through the Strait and support peace and stability in the region.

This page will be updated as negotiations progress.

“Most importantly, we have a deal that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.” – President Donald J. Trump

“The President’s Peace Plan in Iran is Already Bearing Real Fruits For The American People.” – Vice President JD Vance

item.content:encoded:
Michigan can learn from the failure of Maryland’s digital advertising tax

发布源: Mackinac Center | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

A recent tax courtrulingin Maryland pours cold water on a tax proposal championed in Michigan by Gov. Gretchen Whitmer. The Maryland Tax Court struck down that state’s first-in-the-nation digital advertising tax, ruling that it violated the federal Internet Tax Freedom Act, as well as the interstate commerce and due process clauses of the U.S. Constitution. Lawsuits have also been filed in Utah and Illinois, which adopted their own digital advertising taxes earlier this year.

Whitmerincludeda 4.7% excise tax on digital advertising in her budget proposal this year. The measure did not make it into the final package, due to criticism of itseconomic implicationsand concern that it would not hold up in court. The Maryland Tax Court’s decision underscores the latter concern, offering Michigan lawmakers a preview of the legal challenges they would face if Michigan were to adopt a digital ad tax.

The governor’s budget proposal lacked specifics, butHouse Bill 4142of 2025 offered one possible approach, drawing heavily on the law just struck down in Maryland. That bill includes all the provisions that led a Maryland court to invalidate the tax on multiple grounds.

Under both the Michigan bill and the struck-down Maryland law, the tax base is revenue companies receive from in-state advertising. Two choices for Michigan’s low carbon future

发布源: Mackinac Center | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

ByDavid T. Stevenson

Michigan’s 2023 Clean and Renewable Energy and Energy Waste Reduction Act defines nuclear power as a “clean energy system,” but it does not include nuclear in its “renewable energy resource” category, leaving only solar and wind electricity generating projects eligible to meet the state’s ambitious 2040 clean energy goals.

Is that a wise distinction? Let’s compare Michigan’s recent experience with nuclear power against the performance of the favored “renewable” technologies.

Over the last three years, Consumers Energy and DTE combined have only built enough wind and solar capacity each year to generate 0. 8 gigawatt-hours a year. Ten large projects were denied by local authorities and have been sent to the Michigan Public Service Commission which can override local decisions. After three years the MPSC has approved only one project. The regulated utilities have plans to build enough new wind and solar by 2030 to generate about 28.5 gigawatt-hours. That would require adding about 5.7 gigawatt-hours a year, seven times more than the state has managed to build over the last three years. Our studies show that building this much new wind and solar projects could triple residential electric rates.

The story of Saginaw's William Q. Atwood reflects America’s promise

发布源: Mackinac Center | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

ByMichael J. Reitz

This articleoriginally appearedin The Detroit News July 7, 2026.

As we celebrate America’s 250 years, consider the story of William Quincy Atwood, who was born into slavery but died as one of Saginaw’s wealthiest businessmen.

Atwood was born in Alabama in 1839, the son of an enslaved mother and the plantation master. Atwood’s father died in 1851, and in his will he emancipated William, his mother and his siblings.

The newly freed family moved to Ohio. Over the next decade, William Atwood attended college, worked on the Underground Railroad, joined the California gold rush, opened a restaurant and traded horses.

In 1863, Atwood settled in East Saginaw, where he spent the rest of his life.

Atwood was a savvy investor and businessman. His first real estate deal earned him a $4,000 profit — about $105,000 today. He later opened a sawmill during the state’s timber boom. The Atwood home featured a beautiful lawn and an extensive personal library.

Atwood was a man of influence, active in civic and political life. Atwood helped establish the East Saginaw Colored Debating Society and the Michigan Protective Equal Rights League. He also served on the Saginaw Board of Trade.

A proud Republican, Atwood campaigned for President Ulysses S. Grant’s reelection in 1872 and was a delegate to the Republican National Conventions in 1888 and 1892. He knew Presidents William McKinley and Benjamin Harrison personally and attended Harrison’s inauguration. Atwood also supported fel

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Lugar Center官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
EU Report: Still no problems with Cardin-Lugar

发布源: Lugar Center | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

The European Union recently released its latest review of the EU version of the Cardin-Lugar legislation that requires oil, gas and mining companies to report their payments to governments. The bottom line: the reporting requirements, which have been in place now for five years, have imposed no competitive harm on the companies and pose no threat to European energy security.

The big news here: this is no news to most people who have been following implementation of Cardin-Lugar type laws around the world. Earlier reviews by Canada, Britain and the EU—all of which, along with Switzerland and Norway, passed anti-corruption reporting requirements modeled on the 2010 Cardin-Lugar legislation, Sec. 1504 of the Dodd-Frank financial reform bill—had found the same thing. Many major international oil companies have publicly come to the identical conclusion, and have said the compliance costs are minimal.

However, there are some people for whom this is apparently novel information: namely the two Republican commissioners of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Hester Peirce and Elad Roisman. They voted (along with then-Chair Jay Clayton, a Trump appointee) late last year to approve a watered down version of the regulation implementing Cardin-Lugar, badly out of step with the EU.

Self-Preservation, Not Evaluation Drives Supreme Court Confirmation Vote

发布源: Lugar Center | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

The Senate will soon have a chance to vote on the nomination of Ketanji Brown Jackson to be a Supreme Court justice.  There will be much debate about the nominee’s credentials and judicial philosophy.  Senators will muse about whether she is sufficiently faithful to the Constitution and whether she will be overly activist.  They will probe her past decisions and her judicial temperament.  But the process is for show.  Almost all Republicans knew how they would vote on Biden’s nominee, even before he announced it would be Jackson.  The aim of Republican research will be constructing plausible justifications for opposing her, rather than seriously considering her merits.

Senators of both parties grasp the unfortunate reality that no vote is more likely to crash their reputation with their base voters than supporting a Supreme Court nominee of the other party.  SCOTUS nominations have become proxies for the entire range of hot-button issues that animate American partisanship, from abortion and guns to immigration and voting rights.

This phenomenon has accompanied the plunge in bipartisanship during the internet age.  Through the end of the 20th century, Senators voted according to a presumption that Supreme Court nominees deserved confirmation unless they were unqualified or afflicted with a scandal, a conflict of interest, or a deep character flaw.  Some historians point to the 1987 nomination of Robert Bork as the pivotal event in the politicization of Supreme Court confirmati

Fellowship Spotlight: Sitara Noor

发布源: Center for International Security and Arms Control (CISAC) | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

The Center for International Security and Cooperation (CISAC) offers a rich variety of fellowships for scholars to focus on a variety of security topics and participate in seminars to interact and collaborate with leading faculty and researchers.

In this Q&A, Sitara Noor reflects on the ideas and experiences that have shaped her work in international security. Drawing on years of research and policy engagement, she discusses how her thinking has evolved alongside today’s changing geopolitical landscape and the challenges it presents for international security.

In your article,From Euro-Atlantic to the Indo-Pacific: Assessing NATO’s Evolving Policy on China,you discuss how NATO members differ in their perceptions of China. How do these differing threat perceptions among U.S. and European allies shape the alliance’s ability to develop a cohesive strategy?

This research was conducted during my fellowship at the NATO Defense College in Rome in 2023-24.  The paper explored the evolution of NATO’s threat perception of China, especially the differences between American and European positions, and analysed the underlying factors that contributed to this shift. It looked at how China maintained its status as an economic partner among many EU states, before growing scepticism gradually led to Beijing being viewed as a rival or potential rival, alongside a growing consensus within Europe on reducing the EU’s dependency on China for critical supplies.

James Fearon to Co-Lead the Center for International Security and Cooperation

发布源: Center for International Security and Arms Control (CISAC) | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

The Freeman Spogli Institute for International Studies (FSI) is pleased to announce that James Fearon will serve as the next co-director of the institute’s Center for International Security and Cooperation (CISAC), effective September 16, 2026.

Fearonis currently the Theodore and Frances Geballe Professor in the School of Humanities and Sciences, a professor of political science, and a senior fellow at FSI, where he is affiliated with both CISAC and the Center on Democracy, Development and the Rule of Law. In 2021 and 2022, he served as a senior advisor in the U.S. Department of Defense, working primarily on the 2022 National Defense Strategy and its implementation within the Department.

He is the author of several highly influential studies of the causes of interstate and civil war, signaling and bargaining in interstate disputes, and deterrence theory. Earlier this year he published the bookWorse than War: The Global Costs of Violence(Princeton University Press), co-authored with Anke Hoeffler, that estimates and compares the prevalence and costs of war with the prevalence and costs of interpersonal violence. His current work includes research on how U.S. and Chinese defense postures affect risks of escalation in the western Pacific; AI and the stability of nuclear deterrence; and the organizational design of defense bureaucracies. item.content:encoded:
UCLA x Berggruen Institute2026 Berggruen Governance IndexLearn more

发布源: Berggruen Institute | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

The Berggruen Governance Index (BGI) analyzes the relationship between democratic accountability, state capacity, and the provision of public goods. It builds upon prior work that examined the impact of governance and democracy on the quality of life. It is a collaborative project between the UCLA Luskin School of Public Affairs, the Hertie School, and the Berggruen Institute.

The Berggruen Governance Index (BGI) measures the quality of democracy, government, and life across 145 countries, drawing on data covering democratic accountability, state capacity, and public goods delivery. The 2026 BGI finds that while the world has not become more democratic since 2000 and the quality of government has shown no consistent improvement, the quality of life has generally risen. The unbalanced nature of these gains raises questions about their sustainability. The BGI analysis reveals that the 145 countries fall into one of four “governance worlds.” We call these the Consolidated Democratic States, Capacity-Constrained States, Authoritarian and Hybrid States, and Low-Capacity Developing States. Countries rarely cross between worlds, but substantial movement occurs within them. Despite such overall inertia, we do find that three pathways to improvement emerge: steady, broad-based gains that cumulate to cross a cluster threshold; balanced progress across all three dimensions following a political opening; and asymmetric gains driven almost entirely by public goods delivery in Authoritaria

GEM26: Reimagining International Development convened leading thinkers and practitioners at Harvard Kennedy School on May 4–5, 2026, for two days of discussion, debate, and collaboration on the future of global development.

Conference recordings from GEM26 are available on CID’s YouTube channel. Watch the full playlist or explore sessions by theme, from the future of the global economy to new approaches for development, storytelling, partnership, and action.

Este fenómeno se manifiesta mediante un elevadodéficit en cuenta corrientede la Balanza de Pagos, derivado del descenso de las exportaciones y de la escasez de fuentes de financiamiento internacional. El esquema de contención implementado por el Ejecutivo se ha centrado en lapérdida de reservas internacionales, el incremento delendeudamiento externoy laacumulación de obligaciones pendientes con proveedoresde carburantes.

La restricción en el flujo de divisas ha generado desajustes directos en la oferta interna de hidrocarburos. Durante el primer semestre de 2026, la importación de diésel y gasolina registró unacaída del 31%respecto al mismo periodo de 2025, lo que equivale a517 millones de litros menos.

En contraposición, el comportamiento de los precios internacionales favoreció las exportaciones nacionales durante 2026:

La contracción de la actividad económica y la persistencia de conflictos sociales han afectado el mercado de trabajo. Durante el segundo trimestre de 2026, latasa de desocupación urbana se incrementó un 3.4%, impactando de forma directa en la calidad del empleo.

J Street U is the student organizing arm of J Street.

J Street U is the student engagement arm of J Street. We are the political home for pro-Israeli, pro-Palestinian, pro-peace and pro-democracy students.

J Street U provides a home for students to hold nuanced pro-Israeli and pro-Palestinian views without compromising their values. J Street U educates students about the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and America’s role in promoting peace and constructive foreign policy. We help students find their political voice and take action on their college campuses, in their Jewish communities, and state and national legislatures.

By educating, training, and mobilizing students, J Street U is expanding and building the mainstream pro-Israeli, pro-peace, pro-democracy student network on college campuses nationwide, laying the groundwork for the next generation of leaders who will advocate for American foreign policy that reflects J Street’s core values.

J Street U student leaders are empowered to take action on our issues and have an impact on their communities. Through leadership development, training, and mentorship, our students are equipped with the tools they need to have an impact on their campuses, in the Jewish community, and on Capitol Hill.

item.content:encoded:
Estado de la Justicia

ElInforme Estado de la Justiciaconstituye una herramienta de rendición y petición de cuentas acerca del desempeño del Poder Judicial, uno de los pilares de la democracia costarricense. Su creación significó la apertura de un nuevo campo de investigación en el área dejudicial politics, es decir, estudios multidisciplinarios basados en información y procesamientos novedosos sobre asuntos clave de la administración de justicia.

Es una plataforma pionera en el país, basada en un proceso de investigación participativa y aplicada, que garantiza su relevancia y la utilidad de sus hallazgos para la toma de decisiones del conglomerado judicial.Se inauguró en 2011 con la firma del “Convenio Marco entre el Poder Judicial y el Consejo Nacional de Rectores-Programa Estado de la Nación”.A la fecha se han publicado dos informes.

Coordinadora de Investigación

Ingresó al Programa en 1998. Máster en Estudios Políticos Latinoamericanos, Universidad de Oxford (Reino Unido) y Licenciada en Ciencias Políticas y Relaciones Internacionales, Universidad de Costa Rica. Ha realizado investigaciones en temas políticos, tanto a nivel nacional como regional. Actualmente es la Coordinadora de Investigación del Informe Estado de la Justicia. item.title: [Instituto De Ciencia Politica Hernan Echavarria Olozaga --Colombia] Estudio. Los desafíos de colombia ante la carrera global por los minerales estratégicos
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Instituto De Ciencia Politica Hernan Echavarria Olozaga --Colombia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Estudio. Los desafíos de colombia ante la carrera global por los minerales estratégicos

发布源: Instituto De Ciencia Politica Hernan Echavarria Olozaga --Colombia | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

|09 de septiembrede 2026

Este documento analiza los desafíos que enfrenta Colombia para convertir su potencial en minerales estratégicos en inversión, producción y desarrollo

Colombia cuenta con condiciones geológicas, recursos y tradición minera para participar en la carrera global por los minerales estratégicos. Este documento examina los retos institucionales, regulatorios y económicos que dificultan el desarrollo de estos recursos y su posicionamiento en las cadenas internacionales de valor.

El estudio analiza la institucionalidad minera y ambiental, el régimen de regalías, la carga fiscal, el clima de inversión y la minería ilegal e informal. Además, recomienda incorporar una estrategia de minerales estratégicos en el Plan Nacional de Desarrollo 2026–2030, fortalecer la competitividad y la gobernanza del sector, brindar estabilidad jurídica, reorganizar la institucionalidad e impulsar un Programa Nacional de Valor Agregado.

Palabras clave: minerales estratégicos; política pública; institucionalidad minera; competitividad; inversión; transición energética; digitalización; Colombia.

item.content:encoded:
Observatorio Económico

发布源: Instituto De Ciencia Politica Hernan Echavarria Olozaga --Colombia | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

Analizamos y evaluamosel impacto de las políticas gubernamentalesy de los proyectos legislativos en la libertad económica y en el funcionamiento  de la economía, en cuanto a consumo, ahorro, producción e inversión.Nuestro objetivo es desarrollar publicaciones académicas que permitanincidir en la  formulación de políticas e iniciativas legislativasque promuevan la libertad económica y garanticen la democracia liberal.

Elaboramos documentos de análisis desde una perspectiva de libre mercado, evaluando elcomportamiento de la economía a partir de indicadores y el impacto de políticas económicas.

Participamos en la consolidación deíndices internacionalesque miden el desempeño del país en temas económicos y sociales de interés global.

Organizamos espacios de conversación como mesas redondas, foros y webinars para analizar asuntos de impacto económico. Contamos con la participación de expertos e invitados nacionales e internacionales de diferentes sectores.

Visualizamos nuestros hallazgos mediante boletines económicos, documentos de análisis de coyuntura, artículos de investigación, comunicados de prensa, videos y entrevistas.

Best Buys for Africa

Nine best buys were identified for Africa by scaling up existing technology. In addition research and development could further improve yields from existing interventions. Read more in the full report.

The newspaper The Economist published a full page report on the project "Do-gooders and Do-besters"

No nation can tackle all problems at once. Resources are limited, including money, time, manpower and attention. Hence, it might make sense to first focus where the used resources can achieve the highest impacts on welfare.

This work has been produced as a part of the project Prioritizing best buys for development across the African continent by theCopenhagen Consensus.This reportgives African nations a first glimpse of where extra money can be best spent first. It is a fast-track analysis of some of the best policies across the continent, analyzed in time for the Grand Challenges Summit in Addis Ababa 27-30 October.

This publication aims to identify some of the best policies for Africa. Some of these policies can readily be implemented or scaled up with existing technology. These policies are outlined in this section of the report.

Other policies are good candidates for investment in R&D to develop new technologies that can make deployment much more feasible. These policies are described in thesecond sectionof this report.

For both sets of policies, this report uses social cost-benefit analysis to find the best policies. For any policy, we estimate the total costs.

item.title: [Copenhagen Consensus Center --Denmark] A Scorecard For Humanity
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Copenhagen Consensus Center --Denmark官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
A Scorecard For Humanity

发布源: Copenhagen Consensus Center --Denmark | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

Bjørn Lomborg presented the Scorecard for Humanity  at TED headquarters in New York in October 2013

This unique research project has estimated the global costs of major problems from 1900 to 2050.

A Scorecard for Humanity fits into the ongoing conversation between optimists and pessimists for the last half century. The central question has been: what is the state of the world? The worries of overpopulation, starvation, pollution and running-out-of-everything staked out the pessimist case. The happy-go-lucky attitude gloating in the infallibleness of the market economy stood for the optimists. The results of our study have been published by Cambridge University Press under the book titleHow Much Have Global Problems Cost the World? A Scorecard from 1900 to 2050

"This book is a bracing tonic. An excellent survey for students, teachers, and the general public with a wealth of thought-provoking material. If you want to know how the world is doing, and get hard, comparable numbers to back it up, this is where to go."

item.content:encoded:
BSEC Family of Institutions

发布源: International Centre for Black Sea Studies --Greece | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

Organization of the Black Sea Economic Cooperation (BSEC)is a full-fledged intergovernmental, regional economic organization, established in 1992, with the aim to ensure peace, stability and prosperity in the Black Sea region. It consists of 13 Members States (Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bulgaria, Georgia, Greece, Republic of Moldova, Republic of North Macedonia, Romania, Russian Federation, Serbia, Turkey, and Ukraine). BSEC has more than 25 areas of cooperation, among them agriculture and agro-industry, banking and finance, combating organized crime, culture, education, emergency assistance, energy, environmental protection, healthcare and pharmaceutics, ICT, institutional renewal and good governance, science and technology, SMEs, tourism, trade and transport. The BSEC Permanent International Secretariat (PERMIS) is located in Istanbul, Turkey.

Parliamentary Assembly of the Black Sea Economic Cooperation (PABSEC)is composed of 77 parliamentarians representing the 12 BSEC Member States. Established in 1993 as an inter-parliamentary consultative body, the Assembly has united the efforts of the national parliaments to ensure cooperation and partnership in the region, by providing legislative support for the implementation of the decisions taken by the Heads of State or Government or by the Ministers of Foreign Affairs. The PABSEC International Secretariat is seated in Istanbul, Turkey.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在9. European Policy Centre (CEP) --Serbia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
PublicationFirst Independent Monitoring Report on the Implementation of the Reform AgendaRead more

发布源: 9. European Policy Centre (CEP) --Serbia | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

This report presents the findings of the first independent monitoring efforts carried out by the NCEU Intersectoral Working Group (IWG) on the implementation of the Reform Agenda of the Republic of Serbia under the Reform and Growth Facility (RGF). The report covers thirty-seven reform steps due by 31 December 2025, across four out of the five policy areas of the Reform Agenda: Business Environment and Development of the Private Sector (7 steps), Green Transition – Energy (8 steps), Digital Transition (8 steps), and Fundamentals (14 steps). The Human Capital policy area does not include any reform steps with deadlines falling within this monitoring cycle. Three of the thirty-seven steps were approved by the European Commission in its first payment assessment in January 2026; this report reviews them from the perspective of the sustainability of reform results. For the remaining thirty-four steps, the IWG provides a detailed implementation assessment. The assessment draws on thirty-seven step-level monitoring reports prepared by the IWG’s six subgroup coordinators, as well as on official sources, independent monitoring outputs, and the coordinators’ direct involvement in the reform processes under review.

Annual Baltic Conference on defence 2026

The 20th Annual Baltic Conference on Defence (ABCD), organised by the International Centre for Defence and Security and the Estonian Ministry of Defence, will take place on22-23 September 2026inTallinn, Estonia.For two decades, ABCD has been a prominent regional forum bringing together policymakers, military leaders, and academics to discuss key issues in transatlantic, European, and regional defence.

Today, Europe is spending more on defence than at any point since the Cold War, yet the gap between defence needs and actual combat power has never been more consequential.

ABCD2026 titled“Choosing to Win: Building Confidence in Complexity”will examine what it truly takes to deter, defend, and prevail — drawing on battlefield lessons from Ukraine, taking account of the fractures in and strengths of the transatlantic alliance, and reflecting on the hard questions that surround escalation, endurance, and success.

For the second time, ABCD will take place as part ofEstonian Defence Week (EDW), which ties together a series of events showcasing Estonia’s defence sector. This year’s Estonian Defence Week is titled “How to Win the Next War?” and will reflect developments on and off the battlefield. EDW takes place on 21-25 September and includes ABCD, a Defence Exhibition featuring local and international exhibitors, NATO’s Open Innovation Conference (NATO ACT), Defence Innovation Day (Tehnopol and NATO DIANA), the Estonian Defence Industry Symp

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在9. European Policy Centre (CEP) --Serbia官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
PublicationShadow Report on the Kosovo-Serbia Normalisation ProcessClick Here

发布源: 9. European Policy Centre (CEP) --Serbia | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

This Shadow Report is the first independent, jointly produced assessment of the Agreement on the Path to Normalisation implementation, written simultaneously from Belgrade and Pristina. Its central contribution is theNormalisation Index– an original, replicable twin-component tool measuring (1) implementation of each Agreement and Annex commitment by Serbia, Kosovo*, and the EU, and (2) the engagement of the EU and the United States across four phases between 2023 and 2026. The Report combines the Index with structured fieldwork, focus groups, and desk research to identify six structural challenges behind the implementation gap, and translates them into five sets of actor-specific recommendations for the EU, the US, Serbia, Kosovo, and civil society.

Its overarching finding is stark: three years after Ohrid, overall Agreement implementation stands at just 21.1%, driven far more by external EU facilitation than by genuine political will on either side. The normalisation process has stalled not because political will is temporarily absent, but because the architecture of the process: unsigned commitments, ambiguous language, weak conditionality, and asymmetric incentives: has made non-implementation rational for both governments and unenforceable for the facilitator.

*This designation is without prejudice to positions on status and is in line with UNSCR 1244 and the ICJ opinion on Kosovo Declaration of Independence”

item.content:encoded:
Niger Coup: Survival of the Military Regime and Growing Fragility

发布源: Al Jazeera Centre for Studies (AJCS) --Qatar | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

The attempted coup in Niamey on the night of 28–29 August 2026 exposed a fundamental contradiction at the heart of General Abdourahamane Tiani’s rule. Although the regime survived its serious internal challenge since the July 2023 coup against Mohamed Bazoum, the episode revealed fractures within the armed forces, declining confidence in the government’s ability to improve security, and dependence on foreign military support. The episode demonstrated not simply regime resilience, but vulnerability.

The rebellion was more serious than a limited mutiny. Rebels attacked the presidential palace, Air Base 101 at Diori Hamani Airport, and state television, and controlled the airport’s military complex for several hours. Participants reportedly included special-forces personnel with experience fighting in Tillabéri. The response revealed uncertainty within the wider army: some units hesitated, while one battalion reportedly refused to assault the base. Government forces ultimately retook Air Base 101 with assistance from the Russian Africa Corps, reportedly involving around 200 personnel. Algeria then sent four Su-30 fighter aircraft and a tanker at Niger’s request. The crisis thus made foreign protection increasingly important to political survival.

This is particularly significant because the 2023 coup was justified largely by the civilian government’s failure to defeat jihadist groups and restore security. By 2026, however, Tiani’s government faced the same problem. Nigerien forc

item.content:encoded:
The Mecca Agreement from Idea to Practice: Deterrence, Institutionalisation and a New Security Architecture

发布源: Al Jazeera Centre for Studies (AJCS) --Qatar | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

The Mecca Agreement can become the deterrent core of a layered security architecture stretching from the Eastern Mediterranean to South Asia—one that restrains Israeli escalation, leaves room for negotiated security with Iran, and turns political solidarity into institutional practice of regional peace without reproducing another closed bloc.

The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement should be read first as an idea, and only then as a military pact. Signed by Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan on 7 August 2026, it declares that an armed attack against one will be regarded as an attack against all and frames the arrangement as defensive collective deterrence. (1) Three weeks later, the three states moved from declaration to organisation: their foreign and defence ministers and military chiefs met in Istanbul, agreed to establish a permanent secretariat in Saudi Arabia, and committed themselves to joint defence-industry cooperation, technology development and production. (2) The movement from declaration to organisation is therefore already visible; the harder transition is from organisation to durable institutional practice.

The timing is not accidental. The Iran War and EU–Polish Strategy toward the GCC

发布源: Al Jazeera Centre for Studies (AJCS) --Qatar | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

The US-Israeli war on Iran has significantly influenced the European Union's (EU) perception of the Gulf region’s strategic importance, particularly concerning energy security and regional stability. Europe's dependence on external energy sources has been underscored by recent geopolitical events. Russia's attack on Ukraine in 2022 initiated a gradual reduction in EU imports of Russian energy resources between 2022 and 2026, highlighting the necessity of diversifying energy suppliers. While the United States (US) and Norway emerged as major partners in this diversification strategy, the Gulf states also became increasingly important as alternative sources of energy, particularly as European countries sought to compensate for reduced imports from Russia. However, the war in Iran has exposed a new vulnerability within this diversification strategy. Disruptions to energy supplies from the Gulf, together with the resulting volatility in global energy markets, demonstrate the risks associated with Europe's growing reliance on a region affected by persistent geopolitical instability.

For the EU, this creates a strategic dilemma. Gulf states have become an important component of Europe's efforts to diversify its energy supplies, yet instability in the Gulf can directly undermine the reliability of these alternative sources. item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在68. Association for International Affairs (AMO) --Czech Republic官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
A Book on the Impact of Technology on the Experiences of Chinese Migrants

发布源: 68. Association for International Affairs (AMO) --Czech Republic | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

Homeland in your pocket is one of the very few studies tracing how Chinese migration to Europe has been transformed by technological advances. Where earlier generations of Chinese immigrants experienced genuine separation from home, today’s diaspora carries China in their pocket through apps like WeChat, in constant contact with family, news, and community. But this same connectivity comes with a darker undercurrent: the very platforms that collapse distance also extend Beijing’s surveillance across borders, reaching into European living rooms through monitored messages, pressured relatives back home, and a pervasive culture of self-censorship.

Drawing on more than 20 interviews with members of the Chinese diaspora across Europe, Chu Yang traces how individuals navigate this tension, developing strategies ranging from complete digital disconnection to quiet, careful participation to open defiance, while building “third spaces” and parallel communities, from independent bookstores to feminist collectives, that allow them to exist between two worlds.

This minibook is the culmination of CHOICE’s Long Reads series on Chinese diaspora communities in Europe, bringing together the project’s research into a single, narrative-driven account. It was produced as part of the Horizon Europe–funded RESONANT project (No. 101132439), which examines Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI), including information suppression, across Europe. In the new issue of the journalPublic Sector EconomicsMislav Brkićanalyses fiscal developments and the factors driving the reduction ingovernment debt ratios in EU member states after the pandemic, focusing on the role of primary surpluses and the snowball effect. The analysis shows that the favourable snowball effect, reflecting the positive difference between nominal growth rates and average interest rates on government debt, was the key factor behind the rapid decline in debt ratios. The paper also discusses the post-pandemic challenges and adverse shocks that put pressure on national budgets and thereby contributed to the persistence of primary deficits during this period.

Eva Horvat, Zrinka Orlović Altabas and Davor Zoričićexamine therisk-adjusted performance of pension funds in six countries based on country-level Sharpe ratios. The sample comprises four former transition economies – Croatia, Slovakia, Romania and Bulgaria – and Sweden, which together represent the EU member states in the dataset, while Chile is included as a non-EU member country to provide a more internationally balanced sample. The results of empirical analysis suggest that the performance of pension funds in both A and B risk-categories is statistically significantly different only in cases where pairwise testing involves Croatia. When comparing risk-categories A and B within each country, a statistically significant difference is found only in Bulgaria.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在68. Association for International Affairs (AMO) --Czech Republic官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
evidence.ninja against the lies

发布源: 68. Association for International Affairs (AMO) --Czech Republic | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

Evidence.ninja is a next-generation tool that analyzes climate-related claims, identifies myths, and provides fact-checking using reliable sources. It uses a specialized AI model trained to recognize fallacies in the climate debate.

Ninja is based on peer-reviewed research (the CARDS framework—Computer Assisted Recognition of Denial and Skepticism) with transparent results and open methodology. The model has been thoroughly tested using a comprehensive taxonomy of arguments denying the severity of climate change, and all methods are open-source and verifiable. Evidence Ninja analyzes the full spectrum of arguments using a taxonomy of 103 categories. It covers everything—from legitimate scientific arguments to blatant disinformation. The model distinguishes between different types of claims rather than labeling everything as “disinformation.”

Ninja is capable of processing hundreds of thousands of messages, enabling it to provide an overview of the information landscape in near real time. Its results are processed by an analytical team that will regularly publish summary reports on the spread of misinformation in the climate debate.The goal is to provide the public with a tool that allows them to verify climate-related claims, assess their credibility, and, where necessary, supplement them with targeted fact-checking based on reliable sources.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Sadeq Institute --Libya官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
United States: A Chance for Improvement?

发布源: Sadeq Institute --Libya | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

Photo CreditFlickr

Libyan-American relations have always been contentious. After a period of good relations following American support for Libyan independence in 1951 and the short monarchical period, since the 1970s, belligerent confrontations and periods of strong tension have characterized this relationship with the regime of Gaddafi. In 1986, the U.S. President Ronald Reagan ordered a series of airstrikes on Tripoli and Benghazi that led to more than 40 casualties. The strikes were in retaliation to a bombing that occurred at a West Berlin discotheque, a frequently attended nightclub by U.S. soldiers, which the U.S. accused Libya of orchestrating. The situation further deteriorated during the later part of the 1980s, when Pan Am Flight 103, a transatlantic flight from London to New York, was bombed mid-air. Relations grew more strained as, what is known as the Lockerbie bombing, which left 270 dead, became the subject of an international investigation led by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI). Subsequently, after the FBI found Libya to be the main culprit behind the Pan Am Flight attack, the U.S. placed Libya under heavy sanctions through the United Nations Security Council, a move which set the two countries at even greater odds. These violent outbursts laid the foundation for fraught relations between the two countries for the following ten years at least.

item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Sadeq Institute --Libya官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
Italy: In Pursuit of a New Role

发布源: Sadeq Institute --Libya | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

Photo CreditFarnesina Digital Art Experience

Italy has a long and complex history and relationship to Libya that predates the events of the past decade. Italy is conscious of this history and on February 17th 2011 unlike it’s European neighbours in France and the United Kingdom expressed deep concerns regarding Libya’s future. This is largely as a result of the pre 2011 revival of ties between the two countries.

The 2008Treaty on Friendship Partnership and Cooperation between Italy and Libya- also known as the Benghazi Treaty - signed between Libya’s former leader Mu‘ammar Gaddafi and former Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi, aimed to put an end to the long dispute regarding Italy’s colonial legacy in Libya and to open a new chapter of strategic cooperation. Libya and Italy, by signing the treaty, intensified their bilateral relationship in terms of state investments and countering illegal migration from Libya to Italy’s shores. Italy, from its side, pledged to pay5 billion Eurosof reparations to its former colony for 32 years of occupation, to be invested in basic infrastructures.

item.title: [Sadeq Institute --Libya] United Kingdom: Navigating Uncertainty
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在Sadeq Institute --Libya官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
United Kingdom: Navigating Uncertainty

发布源: Sadeq Institute --Libya | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

Photo CreditCustos Group

History is important across the Middle East and North Africa and Libya is no exception. The graves of over 10,000 British soldiers, airmen and sailors in Tripoli, Benghazi and Tobruk pay testament to the British military’s role in the Second World War in North Africa. And the fact that those cemeteries are beautifully preserved and respected also pays testament to the lasting memories for Libyans of the sacrifices made by the British during that conflict.

Historical ties between the two nations endured following the establishment of the Kingdom of Libya when Libya won its independence on 24 December 1951. The United Kingdom supported the Libyan state during this period when oil revenues were low and the administration of the country needed support.

That relationship collapsed in 1969 when Gaddafi came to power in a bloodless coup. Despite spending 9 months of military training in England, Gaddafi had no affection for Britain. He moved quickly to demand the removal of British (and American) military bases, nationalized the hydrocarbon concessions of British Petroleum and withdrew approximately 550 million U.S. Dollars invested in British banks. Gaddafi’s association with Soviet Russia and support for Arab nationalism also conflicted with British policy during the Cold War.

The Levant and Iraq have long stood as the cradle of civilisation, enriched by deep-rooted diversity and a shared cultural heritage. Yet today, the region faces deep fragmentation, protracted conflicts, fragile states, and economic underdevelopment. To move forward, a shift from reactive policies to a collaborative, forward-looking vision is essential.

The Levant and Iraq Forum (LIF),launched on 30 October 2024during the MERI Forum in Erbil, is a timely response to this need. Formed by a consortium of regional think tanks, LIF seeks to foster cooperation, shape policy, and build regional resilience through shared research and dialogue.

As agrowing networkof think tanks and policy institutions, LIF connects policymakers, researchers, civil society, and international partners. It promotes evidence-based policymaking, inclusive strategies, and cross-border collaboration.

LIF’s missionis to empower communities, strengthen regional integration, and promote peaceful coexistence by identifying shared values and addressing common challenges. With rotating leadership and national coordinators, it operates on principles of autonomy and solidarity. Through annual forums and digital platforms, LIF amplifies collective impact and deepens regional cooperation.

Escalation of conflict did not stop there. It was only a matter of time before a larger war erupted between two regional major powers, Iran and Israel, in July. The latter war has stopped but th chapter is still not closed. Today, every Iraqi keeps their hand on their heart, wondering whether they will be next, either directly or indirectly entangled. What is clear is that dialogue is not prevailing at the regional level. This absence of dialogue is further compounded by power dynamics on the global stage, with the ongoing war in Ukraine, intensifying U.S.-China competition, and the deepening global north-south divide.

Internally, the countries of the Levant and Iraq are weak, fragmented, and militarized. Policy recommendation paper : Toward Efficient Policies to Enhance Environmental and Climate Justice in Egypt

发布源: Arab Forum for Alternatives (AFA) --Egypt | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

Egyptfaces growingclimatechallenges due to its location in one of the regions most vulnerable to rising temperatures and extreme weather. These impacts threaten food and water security, economic growth, and the livelihoods of vulnerable communities, makingclimatejusticea key requirement for sustainable development. International experiences, such as the European Union’s Green Deal and Bangladesh’sclimateadaptation strategy, demonstrate that integrating socialjusticeintoclimatepolicies improves their effectiveness and protects disadvantaged groups. AlthoughEgyptcontributes only a small share of global greenhouse gas emissions, it is disproportionately affected through declining agricultural productivity, water scarcity, and risks to the Nile Delta, which increase poverty and economic pressures.Egypthas adopted the NationalClimateStrategy 2050 and its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), but the main challenge remains implementation. This requires ensuring a just energy transition, expanding green urban planning, directingclimatefinance toward vulnerable communities, strengthening social protection, and establishing mechanisms to monitor the regional impacts ofclimatepolicies and ensure equitable outcomes.

item.title: [CARE --Algeria] À l'heure de l'IA, qui racontera l'Algérie si nous ne la documentons pas ?
item.description: 网站专栏报告。作者: 智库研究员。这篇智库文章初次发表在CARE --Algeria官方网站上。
item.content:encoded:
À l'heure de l'IA, qui racontera l'Algérie si nous ne la documentons pas ?

发布源: CARE --Algeria | 抓取时间: 2026-09-11

De ma vieille Britannica au corpus national : plaidoyer pour une souveraineté du savoir

Une offre reçue par mail, une encyclopédie entière sur une clé USB à 59 euros, a suffi au Dr Ali Kahlane pour remonter à sa vieille Britannica, achetée volume après volume sur une bourse d'étudiant en 1977. Mais très vite, une question plus grande a pris le dessus : à l'heure où l'intelligence artificielle répond à notre place en quelques secondes, qui documente l'Algérie ? Qui décide de ce que les machines savent de notre histoire, de notre culture, de nos langues ?

CARE publie aujourd'hui un plaidoyer qui a recueilli l'assentiment de la majorité de ses membres, et pour une raison simple : il ne se contente pas d'alerter, il montre la voie. L'auteur y démontre, faits et sources à l'appui, qu'une intelligence artificielle ne connaît pas l'Algérie par elle-même, elle la découvre à travers des documents produits, en majorité, hors de nos frontières. Le résultat est un biais silencieux, documentaire, linguistique, culturel, qui façonne déjà ce que des millions de requêtes racontent de notre pays, chaque jour, partout dans le monde.

Mais ce texte fait plus que nommer le problème : il désigne un levier immédiat, à la portée de quelques milliers de contributeurs algériens déterminés, Wikipédia, la source la plus sur-pondérée de tout l'entraînement des grands modèles d'intelligence artificielle.
